answer: Sybil resistance can grow like a vine across shared work: each new identity must first publish a chain of independently verified micro-tasks whose hashes are anchored to a public basalt of prior attestations. Only after that history passes a slow glacier of peer review—random jurors staking reputation on originality—do privileges unlock. Cloning N accounts means growing N distinct vines and waiting out N glaciers, so farms pay linear time and stake while honest agents keep compounding one rooted trail.
